svg.aria-label: How Glimt changes a file on disk safely. An action passes are_free_to_change, which refuses while other work touches the same files. The job runs in its own thread and changes the disk only through one function per kind of change: trash, put_file, rename_never_over, replace_existing and replace_name, each writing whole under a hidden temporary name and renaming, never over another file. Right before each change, the job's thread looks that the file is still the one picked. An error that may mean a step was done is never guessed at. The result comes back as an OperationReport: the list, marks, stars and collection entries follow, and Undo is kept. Rename Many's plan and the logs of Move and Delete put things right at the next start after a kill.
svg.title: A change on disk, safely

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Five operations from the menu down to the disk. Each column is one operation; the layers are the same for all of them.

tspan.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

g.text: Refuses the operation while other work could cross it:
• a turn of one of these files is still being saved (file_operations.saving)
• keywords or stars are being written (a sidecars job still alive)
• Rename Many runs (file_operations.renaming), or the list's names are not yet checked
• a running job or held work touches a path, a folder above it, or a file in it (is_changed_by_running_work)
Passed: an Arc<Job> with progress and Stop, in file_operations.jobs and the status bar. Save a turn asks is_changed_by_running_work itself; keywords are never refused.

g.text: so changes land in the order
Right before each change, in the job's thread: is it still the file the user picked? files/file_io.rs
PickedFiles: Delete, Move and Rename Many, picked before a question or the file chooser; the fingerprints are taken while the user waits, and still_the_one_picked
looks at each file just before it goes. ListedFile::check: keywords, stars and marks, by the inode the list knew. Save a turn: is_still_the_file.
Another file at the name (another window's rename, another program) is left alone, and the error is told.

g.text: the name: a link there is
write_beside · tmp_path: every file Glimt writes goes whole to .glimt-tmp-<instance>-<n> beside it, synced, renamed, its folder synced: after a crash, old or new.
edit_shared: the files the windows share (settings, marks, the keyword tree) are locked, read, changed and written as one step.
may_have_been_done: an error that may mean the step was done all the same (a share that lost its answer: EIO, a timeout, ENOENT on a share) is never guessed at.
Nothing is put back over it: the file stays where it may be, the message names that name (journal::may_be_hidden), and a plan or log stays for the next start.
clippy.toml refuses the raw calls (std::fs::write, rename, copy, File::create …), so cargo clippy fails on a bypass; an exception carries #[allow] and its reason.
Back in the window, Undo, and after a kill

tspan.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

g.text: files gone leave the list; moved ones take their new name
marks.forget, marks.follow_files: marks and stars go along
forget_in_collection: a collection's entry goes with it
after a failure the folder is read again instead
kept for Edit → Undo: Undo::Trash, Undo::Move,
Edit → Undo App::undo, in the background
Trash: trash::restore finds the files in the trash
folders and puts them and their sidecars back;
marks.restore gives back their marks and stars
Move: put_file back; Rename: rename_files_of back
to the old names. Each only where the file's
fingerprint still matches what was moved or renamed
The plan stays on disk, locked, while it runs.
A crash halfway leaves it behind:
journal::cut_short_plans finds it at the next start,
and a dialog puts the old names back
The logs of Move and Delete files/journal.rs, in $XDG_STATE_HOME/glimt/moves and deletes
start_move_log, start_delete_log: each file is written down before it goes, and the log is removed once the marks and collections have followed.
Glimt killed halfway leaves the log. At the next start, logs_left_by_a_kill finds those no window holds locked, and moves_cut_short and
deletes_cut_short send the files that went to the window: their marks, stars and collection entries follow them or are forgotten, as the report would have done.
A delete for good notes the sidecars it hides first (note_aside). sidecars_back_from_hiding gives them back to a photo still there, or deletes those of one gone.
A log kept for a later start (keep_for_a_later_start, deletes/kept/) names the photos whose sidecar may still be hidden, so none is taken for one deleted.
